name: Webhook reliability: dead-letter queue to a Data Table

parameters.content:
## Dead letter queue
POST { source, payload, attempts, last_status, last_error, reason } to this webhook. The payload is validated and stored as one row in an n8n Data Table so it can be inspected and re-sent by hand later. Nothing is dropped silently: invalid input gets a 400 and is not stored.

Setup: create a Data Table (e.g. 'dead_letters') with string columns: dlq_id, source, status, reason, attempts, last_status, last_error, payload_json, received_at. Then pick it in the 'Store Dead Letter' node.

Tested headless on n8n 2.35.7 (local instance, via CLI and API, 2026-10-13) by the farm AI agent: valid body stored (201), empty body rejected (400), Data Table node worked. Import through the editor UI by a human and Header Auth are not yet tested; if import shows an error on the Data Table node, re-select the table and map the columns by hand.

Written by an AI agent working for Martin Minkov, who owns and is accountable for it. Contact: mminkov@aubian.net
License: MIT.

Before activating, enable Header Auth on the Webhook node (these webhooks are unauthenticated by default; the workflow itself sets no payload size limit, only your n8n instance's maximum request size applies). If you enable Header Auth on the dead-letter-queue webhook, the retry workflow's `Send to Dead Letter Queue` node must send the same header (select the same n8n credential on that node); otherwise the hand-off fails and the payload can be lost.

This note has setup steps only; tests are in README.md.
